metadata.note: The Detroit and Mackinac Railway (the 'Turtle Line') and two predecessors with their own passenger trains, the Alpena and Northern Railroad and the Au Sable and Northwestern Railway, drawn from the research report research/branches/detroit_and_mackinac_railway.txt (2026-11-02) on 2026-11-02. Before this layer the D&M itself was not drawn at all. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn. The D&M's own predecessor the Detroit, Bay City and Alpena (1883-1894) stays in detroit_bay_city_alpena.geojson, corrected the same day. Each era is drawn on its own alignment: the 1895-1896 Alger connection (dm-alger-emery-jct) until the Sep 1896 Bay City extension (dm-bay-city-national-city), and the 1895-1901 inland line via Lincoln (dm-lincoln-inland-main) until the Dec 1901 Harrisville cut-off (dm-harrisville-cutoff, 1902-1951). Three companies, three colours (Rule 4); ownership splits at DBC&A -> D&M 1894/95, A&N -> D&M 16 Apr 1895 and AS&NW -> D&M lease 1912. Not splits: McHarg stock control 1902; GTW through cars 1950-51 worked by D&M crews; D&M tenancy of the MC Cheboygan union station from 1920.
sources: https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/michiganrrs2lwrp.pdf (John Fowler, Michigan Railroads (2), Lower Peninsula, entries 59-69 Detroit & Mackinac; x/y/z/q/e/f = 1858/1875/1893/1884/1976 Guides/Amtrak; <year>G = that year's Official Guide)
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt), p.258 D&M: every table 'Freight Service only'
metadata.geometry_method: Routed with opstrace.py over cached OSM degree tiles (mail.ru Overpass mirror), OSM ways named or old_railway_operator-tagged 'Detroit and Mackinac Railway' (active Lake State Railway track and abandoned grade, incl. the North Eastern State Trail), plus OSM abandoned/historic ways and OpenHistoricalMap (CC0) railway ways for lifted stretches. Waypoints Nominatim-geocoded and type-checked (Oscoda, Alpena and Cheboygan returned counties and were hand-pinned). Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals. Lifted stretches (inland Lincoln line, Alger - Prescott, Rose City branch, AS&NW, A&N Lake May end) rely on OpenHistoricalMap ways traced by their mappers from USGS topographic maps / 3DEP lidar.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Applied at creation (Rule 1): all D&M lines after 31 Mar 1951 (1952 Guide p.258, every table 'Freight Service only'), the ex-Michigan Central Mackinaw Division bought by the D&M in 1976, the Lake State Railway from 1992, the Alabaster / Erie and Michigan spur, the logging and industrial branches (Avery, Rockport, Black Lake, Bloom, Cleveland, Wolverine, Indian River, Tubbs, Gates, dam spurs, AS&NW Tong and Luzerne branches) and the 1878-1883 Lake Huron and Southwestern / Tawas and Bay County logging road are not drawn.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Nothing trimmed (Rule 5): the DBC&A, A&N and AS&NW were steam from the outset.
metadata.colour_choice: New colours picked 2026-11-02, checked programmatically unused by any company in data/: Detroit and Mackinac Railway #7A3B52, Alpena and Northern Railroad #4A5D8C, Au Sable and Northwestern Railway #8C6A3F. The DBC&A keeps #5a7a5a in its own file.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS - dm-northern-division-alpena-tower and dm-northern-division-tower-cheboygan: drawn 1904-1927; both ends [OPEN]. Start bracket 1899-1904 (Onaway/Tower opening conflict, no dated regular train before the 1904 Guide); end bracket 1927-1949 (Wikipedia 'by 1949', uncited). Best next sources: 1930s-40s Official Guides, Cheboygan Daily Tribune / Alpena News 'last train' stories, Thornton, High Iron along the Huron Shore (1982).

OPEN ENDS - asnw-au-sable-comins: drawn 1893-1909, both [OPEN]; pre-1893 passenger service and the line's 1893 extent toward Comins are unproven; exact D&M lease/purchase dates (1912/1914) not on the branch page.
ANCHORS - dm-rose-city-branch 1909 only; an-alpena-lake-may 1893 only. Do not widen.

NOT DRAWN, candidate anchors: Prescott Branch (Emery Jct - Prescott) after 1896, Lincoln Branch (Lincoln Jct - Lincoln) after 1901, Au Gres Branch, D&M Au Sable River (Comins) and Curran branches 1912-1927, Hillman Branch, Rogers City Branch - the only post-1909 evidence is the 1927 EMPLOYEE timetable's 2nd-class trains, which the source only infers were mixed. A 1920s Official Guide or D&M public timetable, or the D&M annual reports at quod.lib.umich.edu (e.g. https://quod.lib.umich.edu/r/railroad/5220454.1921.001), would settle most at once. Curran branch: AS&NW passenger round trip Feb 1907 (OGR-1907-February) - a candidate 1907 anchor the report did not make drawable.
NOT DRAWN: Alpena and Northern La Rocque/Lake May - Valentine Lake (1894 service only promised); D&M Valentine/Hurst branch 1895-1923 (no passenger evidence).

CONFLICTS RECORDED: reorganization 17 Dec 1894 (Wikipedia) vs 1 Jan 1895 (DFP-1895-0101) - D&M drawn from 1895; last train 31 Mar 1951 vs 2 Apr 1951 (DFP report date) - year 1951 either way; Harrisville cut-off 15 Dec 1901 (DMAR-1903) vs '1900' (Lincoln branch header); A&N Alpena - La Rocque 35 mi (Wikipedia) vs MP ~28-29 (MRR-TT-N); Onaway reached 1899 vs 1901 (migenweb).
UNVERIFIED: 'holiday passenger trains in December 1951 due to snow' (MRR-DM summary, uncited) - within 1951, does not move the end year; route unknown.
GEOMETRY: the D&M Bay City terminal (Pere Marquette station per Fowler) and Alpena depot sites are not located; the pre-1901 inland 'Black River' station is placed by mileage only.

properties.geometry_quality: 47.9 mi drawn against 48.8 mi Bay City - National City (Fowler mileposts) documented. No straight-line leg. Bay City - Pinconning follows the OHM-mapped D&M grade (OHM ways 198835140/198826174), which runs 0.4-2.8 km EAST of the Michigan Central Mackinaw Division; the router first put this leg on the MC and was forced back onto the D&M with waypoints at North Bay City, Linwood and Pinconning on the D&M grade, so no part of it is drawn on MC track. Pinconning - National City is on OSM 'Detroit and Mackinac Railway' (Lake State) track. A 0.28 km junction connector joins the National City end to the shared Emery Junction vertex. The Bay City end is drawn at the east-bank river front (about 43.610 N); Fowler places the D&M at the Pere Marquette station, whose exact site is not located here. Nothing is drawn south of Bay City (D&M through cars south of Bay City ran over other roads). This is the alignment of the D&M's own era (opened 1896); no relocation is known.

segments.note: The Bay City extension opened 20 Sep 1896, when the Alger connection with the Michigan Central was given up [MRR-DM]. Last D&M passenger train Alpena - Bay City 31 Mar 1951 [MRR-1951 citing DFP-1951-0402 and MDOT; DSHOP]; MRR-DM's summary gives 2 Apr 1951, the Free Press report date - same year. The Feb 1952 Official Guide prints the D&M's whole page as 'Freight Service only' (consistent). Operator throughout: Henry K. McHarg's 1902 stock control and the Jan 1950 - Mar 1951 Grand Trunk Western through trains 38/39 'worked by D&M crews' are not operator changes. By 1949 reportedly one train each way, sleepers dropped (Wikipedia, uncited there). Freight continued (D&M to 1992, then Lake State Railway) and is not drawn (Rule 1). Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1896 = Bay City extension opened 20 Sep 1896 [MRR-DM]; 1951 = last train 31 Mar 1951 [MRR-1951, DSHOP]; 1952 Guide 'Freight Service only' consistent. Headway NOT sourced. properties.geometry_quality: 32.2 mi drawn against 28.1 mi Lincoln Jct - Black River (Fowler) plus the rejoin to the shore line south of Ossineke documented. No straight-line leg; entirely on the OHM-mapped inland grade via Mikado (West Greenbush), Gustin and Lincoln (West Harrisville). Junction connectors of 0.45 km (Lincoln Jct) and 0.7 km (Ossineke junction) join it to the shore line's vertices. The pre-1901 'Black River' station is taken to lie on this inland line at 27.6 mi from Lincoln Jct (Fowler 28.1), where it nears the Black River, NOT at the later shore village - an inference from the mileage, not a located station. This is the PRE-1901 alignment, drawn only for its era (1895-1901). The Lincoln Jct - Lincoln stub survived as a branch to 1928 but has no confirmed passenger year after 1901 and is not drawn after 1901.

segments.note: The original main line Lincoln Junction - Lincoln - Black River, built 1885-86 (part via the Alger, Smith & Co. logging road) and used by D&M main-line trains until the lakeshore Harrisville cut-off opened 15 Dec 1901; 'the line between Lincoln and Black River is abandoned' 1901 [MRL via MRR-TT-Lincoln]. D&M from the 1894/95 reorganization (collapsed to 1895). After 1901 Lincoln Jct - Lincoln was a branch: the ICC refused abandonment in Mar 1925 and allowed it in 1927, abandoned 2 Jun 1928 - those are abandonment dates, not passenger dates, and the branch's post-1901 passenger years are NOT drawn (unsourced; 1927 employee-timetable 2nd-class trains are only 'likely mixed'). Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: 49.7 mi drawn against about 50.3 mi Alpena - Tower (MRR-TT-N mileposts) documented. No straight-line leg; on the North Eastern State Trail (OSM, old_railway_operator=Detroit and Mackinac Railway) via Cathro, Bolton, Posen, Hawks (La Rocque), Millersburg and Onaway. Tower is the line's nearest vertex to the village (0.7 km). Drawn on the D&M's own alignment (the ex-D&M North Eastern State Trail and OSM-named D&M grade), not on the Michigan Central Mackinaw Division, which lies well west of it; only the last few hundred metres into Cheboygan come close to MC track, where the D&M used the MC union station by lease from 1920.

segments.note: Northern Division, Alpena - Onaway - Tower. [OPEN START] 1904: the first DATED passenger evidence is the 1904 Official Guide (Fowler's '1904G' tag at Austin's Siding, between Millersburg and Onaway). This is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - service may have begun earlier but no source proves it. Do not extend without evidence. The Alpena - La Rocque piece carried Alpena and Northern mixed trains from Nov 1893 (A&N 1893 is drawn separately) and became D&M on 16 Apr 1895; the line reached Onaway (first freight train 28 Mar 1898; 'through Onaway in 1899' vs 'through Onaway and three miles past Tower in 1901' - conflict) and a 1901 newspaper party rode to Tower, a special, not regular service. [OPEN END] 1927: the 1927 D&M employee timetable shows 'one passenger train in each direction, daily except Sunday' to Cheboygan [MRR-CHEB]. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Wikipedia says Alpena - Cheboygan service was discontinued 'by 1949' (uncited); 1947 diesel service 'between Alpena, Rogers City and Cheboygan' with steam-generator RS-2s is suggestive only. Freight continued (abandoned north of Alpena 1989) and is not drawn (Rule 1). Headway (one train each way daily) reflects the 1927 count only; for other years it is an estimate, NOT sourced.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: no source dates the start or the end of passenger service; 1904 = first confirmed year (Fowler 1904G tags), 1927 = last confirmed year (ETT-1927 via MRR-CHEB). Both ends are [OPEN]. (as checked by the research report research/branches/detroit_and_mackinac_railway.txt (2026-11-02); not re-read for this layer)

No straight-line leg; on the North Eastern State Trail via Waveland and Aloha (Mullet Lake) into Cheboygan. Ends at the trail's Cheboygan end about 1 km from the hand-pinned city centre; the Cheboygan Docks 0.7 mi beyond are not drawn. Drawn on the D&M's own alignment (the ex-D&M North Eastern State Trail and OSM-named D&M grade), not on the Michigan Central Mackinaw Division, which lies well west of it; only the last few hundred metres into Cheboygan come close to MC track, where the D&M used the MC union station by lease from 1920. segments.note: Northern Division extension to Cheboygan: track 'within six miles of Cheboygan' 30 Oct 1903 (DFP-1903-1030); the line 'came up to Cheboygan in 1904' [MRR-CHEB]; Fowler's 1904G tags at Waveland and Aloha; 9 Sep 1905 an express left Cheboygan 'at 11:42 a.m. daily for Detroit' (DFP-1905-0909). [OPEN START] 1904. This is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - service may have begun earlier but no source proves it. Do not extend without evidence. [OPEN END] 1927: 'one passenger train in each direction, daily except Sunday' in the 1927 employee timetable [MRR-CHEB]. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Wikipedia says the service was gone 'by 1949' (uncited). From 1920 the D&M used the Michigan Central's Cheboygan union station by lease - station tenancy, not an operator change. D&M advertised Cheboygan as the transfer point to boats for Mackinac Island. Headway reflects the 1927 count only; otherwise an estimate, NOT sourced.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] [OPEN] 1909 is the ONLY proven passenger year: the Michigan Railroad Commission's 1909 report (MCR-1909) says 'There are no passenger stations of any importance on this line with the exception of at Long Lake and Rose City' - i.e. passenger stations in use. Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed; do NOT widen this anchor to look plausible. Built by the DBC&A to Maltby 1886 and extended to Rose City 1893 (no DBC&A-era passenger evidence). ICC abandonment applied for 1926, ordered kept 18 more months in 1927, 'The Rose City branch is abandoned' 1930 - abandonment dates, NOT passenger ends. The 1927 employee timetable's Wed & Sat 2nd-class trains are only 'likely mixed' (inference, not drawn). Mixed-train service; headway is an estimate, NOT sourced.

properties.speed_source: estimated; not computed from any timetable (Rule 3)

No straight-line leg. Alpena - Hawks (La Rocque) shares its geometry with the D&M Northern Division; Hawks - Lake May follows the OHM A&N branch toward Valentine Lake. The A&N's own 1893 alignment as mapped by OHM; no relocation known before 1895. The Lake May end point is approximate (the lake, not a station).

segments.note: [ANCHOR] [OPEN] 1893 is the only proven year. Opened Alpena - La Rocque 18 Nov 1893 [WIKI-AN]; time card 'The northbound train leaves Alpena's DBC&A depot at 7:30 am' (AAN-1893-1206); 'The A&N mixed freight train north of Alpena stops on demand at Cathro, Bolton, Posen, Hoffman', with a 'neat and comfortable' coach, 'already doing a good business in both passenger and freight' (AAN-1893-1220); Lake May reached Dec 1893 (DFP-1893-1218). Service certainly continued into 1894-95, but no other year is confirmed; do NOT widen this anchor. Corporate end 16 Apr 1895 (acquired by the D&M). La Rocque/Lake May - Valentine Lake (1894) is NOT drawn: the only 1894 passenger statement is in the future tense. One mixed train each way; headway is an estimate, NOT sourced.

properties.line: Au Sable and Northwestern: Au Sable – Comins
properties.speed_source: estimated; 3 ft narrow-gauge mixed trains; not computed from any timetable (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap (CC0) railway ways mapped from USGS topographic maps / 3DEP lidar (OHM way 198826216 Au Sable - Glennie, 1890-1927; 'Hardy Grade'; ways 198911113 / 198826225 to Comins), routed with opstrace.py. No OSM trace survives. Glennie, Bissonette and Comins Nominatim-geocoded (types checked); three waypoints placed on OHM way ends. Douglas-Peucker 8 m, trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: 50.2 mi drawn against about 50.6 mi Oscoda - Comins (Fowler); 56.5 mi on the old route (MRR-TT-AuSableRiver) documented. No straight-line leg, but between Glennie and Hardy the router used some OHM ways dated 1900-1901 to bridge gaps between the 1890-1927 ways, so short stretches may be logging spurs rather than the main line. WARNING (Rule 2): the drawn line runs all the way to Comins from 1893, but the only 1893 evidence (Fowler 'z' tags) is at Doane and Batton near the Oscoda end; Comins first appears (as Pingree) in the 1900 Guide. The road was built by the Potts logging company 1886-1891, but how far it carried passengers in 1893 is NOT established. The Curran branch (Hardy - Curran) is not drawn.

segments.note: H. M. Loud's 3 ft gauge Au Sable and Northwestern (ex-Potts logging road, renamed by Oct 1891). [OPEN START] 1893: first CONFIRMED passenger year - Fowler tags Doane and Batton 'z' (1893 Official Guide). This is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - service may have begun earlier but no source proves it. Do not extend without evidence. Also Comins [Pingree] 1900G; Feb 1907 'The AS&NW operates one passenger train round trip on the main line and Curran Branch' (OGR-1907-February); Nov 1909 freight and passengers 'handled in same train with freight and passenger cars on mixed trains' (MCR-1909). [OPEN END] 1909: last CONFIRMED AS&NW passenger year. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. The corporate end is 1912, when the D&M leased the road (bought 1914); D&M-era passenger service (1912-1927) is unproven and NOT drawn. Steam throughout; no animal traction (Rule 5). Headway (one mixed round trip, 1907) is otherwise an estimate, NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1893 = Fowler 'z' tags at Doane and Batton; 1907 = OGR-1907-February; 1909 = MCR-1909 [MRR-TT-AuSableRiver]. Both ends [OPEN]; headway NOT sourced.
